question: What do we call the special property of metals that allows them to be beaten into very thin sheets, like aluminum foil? 🪙
explanation: Great job! Malleability is the superhero property of metals that lets them change shape into flat sheets when hammered, without shattering! 🔨
hint: Think of a word linked to being hammered or shaped.

question: Which property allows copper to be stretched out into long, thin wires for our electronics? 🔌
explanation: Awesome! Ductility is the cool ability of metals to be drawn into wires, making electricity travel right into our homes! 🪢
hint: It sounds a bit like 'duck', but it means stretching into strings!

question: Why are school bells usually made of metal instead of wood? 🏫
explanation: Brilliant! Metals are sonorous, which means they produce a loud, ringing sound when struck. Ding dong! 🔔
hint: Which word means producing a ringing sound?

question: When you look at a brand new gold ring, it shines brightly. What is this metallic shine called? 💍
explanation: Spot on! Lustre is the fancy science word for that beautiful, glowing shine that fresh metals have. ✨
hint: Think of a word that rhymes with 'cluster' and means shiny.

question: Why are cooking pans mostly made of metals like iron or aluminum? 🍳
options: They are good conductors of heat 🔥
answer: They are good conductors of heat 🔥
explanation: Fantastic! Metals allow heat to pass through them quickly, making them perfect for cooking your favorite meals! 🔥
hint: How does the food get hot from the stove?

question: Most metals are solid at room temperature, but there is one sneaky metal that stays liquid! Which one is it? 🌡️
explanation: Excellent! Mercury is the only metal that is liquid at room temperature, which is why it used to be put in thermometers! 🌡️
hint: It is also the name of the planet closest to the sun.

question: If you try to hit a piece of coal (a non-metal) with a hammer, what will happen? 🔨
explanation: Perfect! Non-metals like coal are brittle, meaning they shatter or break easily when you hit them. 💥
hint: Coal isn't malleable like iron.

question: Which of these is a famous non-metal gas that we need to breathe every single day to stay alive? 🫁
explanation: Superb! Oxygen is a non-metal gas that our bodies need to produce energy and keep us going strong! 🌬️
hint: Trees give off this invisible gas.

question: Metals are usually very hard, but there is a metal so soft you can easily cut it with a butter knife! Which one is it? 🔪
explanation: Way to go! Sodium (and potassium) are unique metals that are super soft and can be sliced right open! 🔪
hint: It's part of the chemical name for common table salt.

question: Non-metals are usually bad at conducting electricity. But the dark 'lead' inside your pencil is a non-metal that CAN conduct electricity! What is it called? ✏️
explanation: Awesome job! Graphite is a special form of carbon (a non-metal) that acts like a metal when it comes to conducting electricity! ⚫
hint: It starts with the letter G.

question: Which of these non-metals is actually a liquid at room temperature? 🧪
explanation: Spot on! While Mercury is the liquid metal, Bromine is the unique liquid non-metal! 🟤
hint: It has a reddish-brown color.

question: If you look at most solid non-metals like sulphur or coal, how do they usually appear? 👀
explanation: Great thinking! Most non-metals don't have that metallic lustre, so they look quite dull to our eyes. 🪨
hint: Think about what a piece of charcoal looks like.

question: Which metal is considered the absolute champion of malleability, meaning it can be beaten into the thinnest sheets ever? 👑
explanation: Brilliant! Gold is extremely malleable. A tiny piece of gold can be hammered into a huge, see-through sheet! 🏆
hint: It is yellow, shiny, and very expensive!

question: What is the non-metal that makes up the hardest natural substance on Earth, the diamond? 💎
explanation: Fantastic! Diamond is just a beautifully organized crystal made entirely of the non-metal Carbon! 💎
hint: It's the same element found in coal and pencil lead.

question: Why are the handles of metal cooking pans usually made of plastic or wood? ✋
explanation: Excellent! Non-metals like wood and plastic don't conduct heat well, protecting your hands from getting burned! 🪵
hint: You don't want the heat from the pan to reach your hand.

question: Which non-metal is commonly used on the red heads of matchsticks to help them catch fire? 🔥
explanation: Superb! Phosphorus is a highly reactive non-metal that helps create the spark when you strike a match! 🔴
hint: It starts with a P and loves to burn.

question: What is the best metal conductor of electricity, even better than copper? (Hint: It's too expensive to use for regular house wires!) 🥈
explanation: Perfect! Silver is the number one conductor of heat and electricity, but we use copper because silver is super pricey! 🪙
hint: It is often used for fancy cutlery or second-place medals.

question: Which of these elements is a non-metal gas used to keep bags of potato chips fresh and crispy? 🍟
explanation: Way to go! Nitrogen is an unreactive non-metal gas that fills chip bags to prevent the chips from going stale or getting crushed! 💨
hint: It makes up 78% of the air we breathe.

question: Which lightweight metal is used widely to make the bodies of airplanes? ✈️
explanation: Awesome! Aluminum is strong but very light, making it the perfect metal for things that need to fly! ✈️
hint: You might wrap your sandwich in a foil made of this.

question: Non-metals are generally poor conductors of heat and electricity. What is the science word for 'poor conductor'? 🛑
explanation: Spot on! Insulators block the flow of heat and electricity, keeping us safe from shocks and burns. 🧱
hint: Think of a word that means 'to protect or block'.

question: When iron gets wet and reacts with oxygen, it forms a flaky reddish-brown layer. What is this called? 🍂
explanation: Great job! Rusting happens when iron meets oxygen and moisture, creating iron oxide. 🟫
hint: Old cars and bikes get covered in this if left in the rain.

question: Which yellow-colored non-metal is often used to make gunpowder and fireworks? 🎆
explanation: Brilliant! Sulphur is a brittle, yellow non-metal that is famous for its use in fireworks and having a strange smell! 🟡
hint: It smells a bit like rotten eggs when it burns.

question: What kind of sound do non-metals make when you drop or hit them? 🪵
explanation: Fantastic! Because non-metals are not sonorous, they just make a flat, dull thud when struck. 📦
hint: Imagine dropping a piece of wood on the floor.

question: Which of these is a property of MOST metals? 💪
explanation: Excellent! Metals are usually packed tightly together, giving them high density and making them feel heavy! 🏋️
hint: Think about lifting a big block of iron.

question: Which metal is commonly applied as a protective coating on iron to prevent it from rusting? 🛡️
explanation: Perfect! Coating iron with Zinc is a process called galvanization, acting like a shield against rust! 🛡️
hint: It starts with a Z.

question: Non-metals can exist in different states at room temperature. Which of these is a solid non-metal? 🪨
explanation: Superb! Sulphur is a yellow powder, meaning it is a solid non-metal, while the others are gases! 🟡
hint: It's the yellow one.

question: Most non-metals are dull, but there is one non-metal used as a purple antiseptic that is actually quite shiny! What is it? 🟪
explanation: Way to go! Iodine is an exception to the rule because it is a non-metal that actually has a bit of lustre! 🟣
hint: Doctors sometimes put this on cuts and scrapes.

question: Which non-metal gas is used in water purification plants to kill harmful bacteria in drinking water? 🚰
explanation: Awesome! Chlorine is a powerful non-metal gas that destroys bacteria, keeping our swimming pools and drinking water safe! 🟢
hint: You can usually smell this in swimming pools.

question: If an object breaks easily into powder when hammered, it is most likely a... 🔨
explanation: Spot on! Breaking easily into a powder is called brittleness, a classic sign that the object is a non-metal! 🪨
hint: Metals bend, but these break.

question: What metal is essential in our blood to carry oxygen around our bodies? ❤️
explanation: Great job! Iron is a vital metal found inside our red blood cells in a protein called hemoglobin! 🩸
hint: It's the same metal that rusts, but it's totally safe in your blood!

question: Which of these non-metals is essential for plants to grow and is a major part of fertilizers? 🌱
explanation: Brilliant! Nitrogen is a crucial non-metal nutrient that plants need to grow tall and healthy! 🌾
hint: It makes up most of the Earth's atmosphere.

question: Metals generally have very high melting points. What does this mean? 🔥
options: They need extremely high heat to melt 🌋
answer: They need extremely high heat to melt 🌋
explanation: Fantastic! Because metals have high melting points, you need a super-hot furnace to turn solid iron into liquid iron! 🌋
hint: It takes a LOT of heat.

question: Which of these objects takes advantage of the 'ductility' of a metal? 🎸
explanation: Perfect! Guitar strings are made by drawing metal out into thin wires, which is exactly what ductility is! 🪢
hint: Look for the option that involves wires.

question: What is the most abundant metal found in the Earth's crust? 🌍
explanation: Excellent! Aluminum is the most common metal hiding right beneath our feet in the Earth's crust! ⛏️
hint: It's the lightweight metal used for soda cans.

question: What is the most abundant NON-metal found in the Earth's crust? 🌎
explanation: Superb! Oxygen isn't just in the air; it binds with other elements in the ground, making it the most abundant non-metal in the crust! 🌬️
hint: It is also the gas we breathe.

question: Which property of metals explains why we use copper for electrical wiring in our houses? 🏡
explanation: Way to go! Copper is a fantastic conductor, letting electrical current zoom through it to power our TVs and lights! ⚡
hint: Wires need to carry power.

question: Some non-metals are gases. Which non-metal gas is famously very light and used to make balloons float? 🎈
explanation: Awesome! Helium is a super lightweight non-metal gas that makes party balloons float up to the ceiling! 🎈
hint: It can also make your voice sound funny!

question: When a metal like silver is exposed to air for a long time, it can turn black. What is this process called? 🥄
explanation: Spot on! Tarnishing is a chemical reaction where the surface of a metal loses its shine and gets a dull or dark coating. 🌑
hint: It starts with a T.

question: Which of these is a daily-life example of using a metal's 'malleability'? 🍔
explanation: Great job! Aluminum foil is just aluminum metal that has been beaten completely flat thanks to its malleability! 🌯
hint: Look for the flat sheet!

question: Non-metals are generally poor conductors of electricity. Because of this, what are they often used for? 🧤
explanation: Brilliant! Because non-metals block electricity, we wrap them around metal wires so we can touch the cables safely! 🔌
hint: They keep the electricity inside the wire.

question: What metal is essential for making our bones and teeth strong? 🦷
explanation: Fantastic! Calcium is a metal element that our bodies use to build strong, healthy bones and teeth! 🥛
hint: You get a lot of this from drinking milk.

question: Which of the following describes the 'tensile strength' of metals like iron? 🏗️
options: Ability to hold heavy weights without breaking 🏋️
answer: Ability to hold heavy weights without breaking 🏋️
explanation: Perfect! Tensile strength means the metal is super tough and can hold up heavy things, which is why iron is used in bridges! 🏗️
hint: Think of strength and heavy lifting.

question: Which of these pairs represents a Metal and a Non-metal (in that order)? ⚖️
explanation: Excellent! Copper is a shiny, conducting metal, and Sulphur is a dull, yellow non-metal! 🥉
hint: Find the one that starts with a shiny wire material and ends with a yellow powder.

question: Coal is used as a fuel because it burns easily. What non-metal is coal primarily made of? 🔥
explanation: Superb! Coal is almost entirely made of the non-metal Carbon, which releases a lot of heat when burned! ⚫
hint: It is the same element found in diamonds.

question: If a material is 'sonorous', it is most likely a... 🎶
explanation: Way to go! Sonorous materials ring when you hit them, which is a classic physical property of metals! 🔔
hint: Think of what bells are made of.

question: Which non-metal is a very good conductor of heat but NOT electricity? (Hint: It is sparkly!) 💎
explanation: Awesome! Diamond (a form of carbon) is a non-metal that can actually conduct heat really well, even though it doesn't conduct electricity! 💍
hint: It's the hardest known natural substance.

question: Which metal is highly prized for jewelry because it does NOT react easily with air or water (it doesn't rust or tarnish easily)? 👑
explanation: Spot on! Gold is a 'noble metal' because it is very unreactive, keeping its beautiful shine forever! 🥇
hint: It is yellow and very valuable.

question: We know metals conduct heat. Which of these metals is famously a POOR conductor of heat compared to others? 🛡️
explanation: Great job! While most metals are great conductors, Lead is an exception and is actually a pretty poor conductor of heat! 🪨
hint: It is a very heavy, toxic metal sometimes used in old pipes.

question: Why do we use copper to make statues that stay outside in the weather for years? 🗽
options: It resists heavy corrosion/rusting better than iron 🛡️
answer: It resists heavy corrosion/rusting better than iron 🛡️
explanation: Brilliant! Copper (and its alloys like bronze) stands up well to weather, protecting statues like the Statue of Liberty for centuries! 🛡️
hint: Think about surviving the rain and sun.

question: To summarize, if you find an object that is shiny, rings when hit, and can be bent without breaking, it is most likely a... 🕵️‍♂️
explanation: Fantastic! Lustre, sonority, and malleability are all the classic signs that you are holding a true metal! 🪙
hint: Think of the properties of a coin.
